record.paper_title: Some results and open problems in research on low dimensional organic conductors
record.original_question: How can the analytically derived conductivity of quasi-one-dimensional organic conductors in the one-dimensional Hubbard model, computed with the memory-function method, be reduced to a realistically usable form without losing the dominant physical contributions? In the paper, the exact susceptibility calculation contains about 2700 terms, so the unresolved task is to introduce realistic approximations that keep the main terms in the relevant sums while making the conductivity formula applicable to actual Bechgaard-salt physics.

evidence.quote: As an illustration, note that the sum invoked in the calculation of the susceptibility has about 2700 terms! Obviously, such a result can not be applied.
Therefore the main problem of this calculation was how to introduce realistic approximations in it, so as to make it applicable, and to take into account the main terms in various sums in it.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the one-dimensional Hubbard model with Hamiltonian

  H = -t \sum_{i,\sigma} (c^\dagger_{i,\sigma} c_{i+1,\sigma} + h.c.) + U \sum_i n_{i,\uparrow} n_{i,\downarrow},

used as a model for quasi-one-dimensional organic conductors (such as Bechgaard salts), perturbed by a small umklapp/impurity term that relaxes momentum. Within the memory-function (Mori–Götze–Wölfle) formalism, the optical conductivity has the form

  \sigma(\omega) = \frac{i\,\omega_p^2/(4\pi)}{\omega + M(\omega)},

where the memory function M(\omega) is expressed, to leading order in the perturbation, in terms of a current–current susceptibility \chi(\omega) whose analytic evaluation in this model produces a sum of approximately 2700 distinct terms (arising from products of Fermi factors, single-particle energies, and matrix elements over the Brillouin zone).

Problem. Devise a controlled approximation scheme that reduces the exact 2700-term expression for \chi(\omega), and hence for \sigma(\omega), to a compact closed-form (or low-term) expression having the following properties:

  (i) it retains the dominant contributions in the relevant temperature, frequency and filling regime appropriate to Bechgaard-salt physics;
  (ii) it preserves the leading low-frequency and low-temperature asymptotics of \sigma(\omega) (in particular, the correct power-law behavior of the dc resistivity \rho(T) in the metallic regime);
  (iii) the discarded terms can be bounded by an explicit small parameter (e.g. U/t, the deviation from half-filling, or T/t);
  (iv) the resulting formula is explicit enough to be fitted to experimental optical-conductivity data.

Provide such an approximation scheme together with rigorous estimates on the neglected terms.
artifact.status_search_result: No specific resolution of this problem—producing a tractable, controlled reduction of the ~2700-term memory-function susceptibility for the 1D Hubbard model targeted at Bechgaard-salt phenomenology—was located. The general program of computing optical conductivity in 1D Hubbard / Luttinger-liquid models via memory-function and Bethe-ansatz methods is active, but the specific approximation task as posed appears unresolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.snippet: Discusses memory-function calculation of conductivity in quasi-1D organic conductors and notes the susceptibility sum contains about 2700 terms that cannot be directly applied.
status_evidence.claim: The need for realistic approximations to the 2700-term susceptibility sum is stated as an open task.
